rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blood on the shirt was false because it was not Yusuf's blood.
rows.anchor: بدم هو كذب، لأنه لم يكن دم يوسف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative parses the blood as fabricated, with the verbal noun standing in for a noun.
rows.anchor: بدم مكذوب فيه، فوضع المصدر موضع الاسم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the narrative, the brothers stained the shirt without tearing it, so Yaqub suspected them because a wolf would have torn it.
rows.anchor: لطخوا القميص بالدم ولم يشقوه، فقال يعقوب عليه السلام: كيف أكله الذئب ولم يشق قميصه؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawwalat means that their selves adorned or made their story seem attractive to them.
rows.anchor: سولت} زينت، {لكم أنفسكم أمرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beautiful patience means either that his affair or conduct is beautiful patience.
rows.anchor: معناه: فأمري صبر جميل أو فعلي صبر جميل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes the phrase as Yaqub choosing beautiful patience.
rows.anchor:
جميل.
وقيل: فصبر جميل أختاره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beautiful patience has neither complaint nor despair.
rows.anchor: والصبر الجميل الذي لا شكوى فيه ولا جزع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaqub seeks God's help to endure what they describe falsely.
rows.anchor: أستعين بالله على الصبر، على ما تكذبون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers brought a wolf and claimed it had eaten Yusuf; God made it speak, and it said it had never seen his face.
rows.anchor: فقال له يعقوب: يا ذئب أنت أكلت ولدي وثمرة فؤادي؟ فأنطقه الله عز وجل، فقال: تالله ما رأيت وجه ابنك قط.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the story, the wolf said it had come to visit kin, but the brothers captured it.
rows.anchor: جئت لصلة قرابة [فصادني هؤلاء]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative says Yusuf remained in the well for three days.
rows.anchor: فمكث يوسف في البئر ثلاثة أيام

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: The jussive form of let them pray is governed as a conditional construction.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: هو جزم على الجزاء،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khilal means friendship and close companionship.
rows.anchor: فيه ولا خلال} مخاللة وصداقة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amr, and Yaqub read both nouns in the accusative for general negation; the others read them nominative with nunation.
rows.anchor: [قرأ ابن كثير، وابن عمرو، ويعقوب: "لا بيع فيه ولا خلال" بالنصب فيهما على النفي العام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the rivers easy for people to direct wherever they wish.
rows.anchor: {وسخر لكم الأنهار} ذللها لكم، تجرونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon continually run for people's benefit and do not pause.
rows.anchor: يجريان فيما يعود إلى مصالح العباد ولا يفتران،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the sun and moon's unceasing course is their obedience to God.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس دؤوبهما في طاعة الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day succeed one another in light and darkness, and in decrease and increase.
rows.anchor: يتعاقبان في الضياء والظلمة، والنقصان والزيادة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording means God gave people something from everything they asked for; the second object, thing, is omitted and the wording is partitive.
rows.anchor: شيئا، فحذف الشيء الثاني اكتفاء بدلالة الكلام، على التبعيض.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes every as rhetorical hyperbole meaning some, as in ordinary speech about knowing or giving everything.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو على التكثير نحو قولك: فلان يعلم كل شيء، وآتاه كل الناس، وأنت تعني بعضهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This partitive hyperbole is compared with God opening every kind of door, meaning some kinds.
rows.anchor: نظيره قوله تعالى: {فتحنا عليهم أبواب كل شيء}

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads min with nunation and ma as negative: God gave things people had not asked for.
rows.anchor: الحسن " من كل " بالتنوين {ما} على النفي يعني من كل ما لم تسألوه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's favors cannot be enumerated or fully repaid with gratitude.
rows.anchor: لا تطيقوا عدها ولا القيام بشكرها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person wrongs himself through disobedience and is ungrateful to God for His favor.
rows.anchor: ظالم لنفسه بالمعصية، كافر بربه عز وجل في نعمته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative says the unjust person thanks someone other than the benefactor, while the ungrateful person denies the benefactor.
rows.anchor: الظلوم، الذي يشكر غير من أنعم عليه، والكافر: من يجحد منعمه.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ikrima, and Mujahid identify the enduring good deeds as saying the four phrases of glorification, praise, monotheism, and magnification.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس وعكرمة ومجاهد: هي قول سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر.

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report calls these four phrases the best words.
rows.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "أفضل الكلام أربع كلمات: سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر"

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits that saying the four phrases is dearer to the Prophet than everything on which the sun rises.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لأن أقول سبحان الله

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Said transmits an instruction to increase the enduring good deeds, identified as magnification, tahlil, glorification, praise, and the declaration of God's power; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: "استكثروا من الباقيات الصالحات"

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Said ibn Jubayr, Masruq, and Ibrahim identify the enduring good deeds as the five prayers; another report attributes this view to Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير ومسروق وإبراهيم: "الباقيات الصالحات" هي: الصلوات الخمس.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas identifies the enduring good deeds as righteous actions, also the view of Qatada.
rows.anchor:
ابن عباس (4) .
وعنه رواية أخرى: أنها الأعمال الصالحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Better reward means better recompense from God; better hope means what a person hopes for.
rows.anchor: {خير عند ربك ثوابا} أي جزاء المراد {وخير أملا} أي ما يأمله الإنسان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asked Shuayb to return from Midian to Egypt to visit his mother and sister; Shuayb allowed him to leave with family and possessions.
rows.anchor: استأذن شعيبا في الرجوع من مدين إلى مصر لزيارة والدته وأخته، فأذن له فخرج بأهله وماله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says winter travel on a detour to avoid Syrian rulers; Moses's wife was ill, they lost their way in a freezing dark night, she went into labor, and his flint would not spark.
rows.anchor: وكانت أيام الشتاء، وأخذ على غير الطريق مخافة ملوك الشام، وامرأته في سقمها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says Moses, jealous over his wife, traveled with caravans at night and apart by day; lost on a cold dark night, he saw fire after his flint failed, as God intended to honor him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن موسى كان رجلا غيورا فكان يصحب الرفقة بالليل ويفارقهم بالنهار،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amkuthu means stay or remain; Hamza reads the hā with damma here and in al-Qasas.
rows.anchor: أقيموا، قرأ حمزة بضم الهاء هاهنا وفي القصص،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anastu means I saw; a qabs is a flame or piece of fire carried on a stick from a larger fire.
rows.anchor: {إني آنست} أي: أبصرت، {نارا لعلي آتيكم منها بقبس} شعلة من نار،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hudan means someone at the fire who can guide Moses to the road.
rows.anchor: {أو أجد على النار هدى} أي: أجد عند النار من يدلني على الطريق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the fire Moses saw a green tree surrounded from bottom to top by brilliant white fire, neither changing the other's color or light.
rows.anchor: رأى شجرة خضراء من أسفلها [إلى أعلاها، أطافت بها نار بيضاء تتقد

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud identifies the tree as a green samura.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مسعود: كانت الشجرة سمرة خضراء.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada, Muqatil, and al-Kalbi identify the tree as al-awsaj.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة، ومقاتل، والكلبي: كانت من العوسج.

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb identifies the tree as al-aliq.
rows.anchor: وقال وهب: كانت من العليق.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas identifies the tree as a jujube tree.
rows.anchor: شجرة العناب، روي ذلك عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The exegetes say Moses saw light rather than fire; it is called fire because he thought it was fire.
rows.anchor: قال أهل التفسير: لم يكن الذي رآه موسى نارا بل كان نورا، ذكر بلفظ النار لأن موسى حسبه نارا.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Most exegetes, including Ibn Abbas and Ikrima, say it was the light of the Lord.
rows.anchor: وقال أكثر المفسرين: إنه نور الرب عز وجل، وهو قول ابن عباس، وعكرمة، وغيرهما.

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Said ibn Jubayr says it was actual fire and one of God's veils; a report from Abu Musa says the fire veil would burn creation as far as God's sight reaches if lifted.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: هي النار بعينها، وهي إحدى حجب الله تعالى،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas via Ata, Hasan, and Qatada say lahw means a woman; Baghawi considers this likelier because intercourse is called play in Arabic and a woman is its locus.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: اللهو المرأة، وهو قول الحسن وقتادة،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas via al-Kalbi says lahw means a child, as does al-Suddi.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: اللهو المرأة، وهو قول الحسن وقتادة، وقال في رواية الكلبي: اللهو الولد، وهو قول السدي،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The woman interpretation is more apparent because intercourse is called lahw in Arabic and a woman is its locus.
rows.anchor: وهو في المرأة أظهر لأن الوطء يسمى لهوا في اللغة، والمرأة محل الوطء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God had taken a wife, it would have been from the heavenly maidens, not earthly people.
rows.anchor: {لاتخذناه من لدنا} أي من عندنا من الحور العين لا من عندكم من أهل الأرض.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says that if this were possible for God, He would have concealed it rather than let people see it.
rows.anchor: لو كان جائزا ذلك في صفته لم يتخذه بحيث يظهر لهم ويستر ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response addresses Christians' claims about Jesus and his mother: a man's wife and child are with him, not someone else.
rows.anchor: أن النصارى لما قالوا في المسيح وأمه ما قالوا رد الله عليهم بهذا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada, Muqatil, and Ibn Jurayj take in as negation: God did not do this.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة ومقاتل وابن جريج: {إن} للنفي، أي: ما كنا فاعلين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative reads the clause conditionally: even if God did such a thing, He would take it from His own realm, but He did not because it is unfitting to divinity.
rows.anchor: وقيل: {إن كنا فاعلين} للشرط أي إن كنا ممن يفعل ذلك لاتخذناه من لدنا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bal turns away from their statement as a lie and falsehood; naqdhif means throw or unleash, and haqq means faith.
rows.anchor: {بل} أي دع ذلك الذي قالوا فإنه كذب وباطل، {نقذف} نرمي ونسلط، {بالحق} بالإيمان،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative identifies the truth as God's word that He has no child, and falsehood as their claim that He took a child.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الحق قول الله، أنه لا ولد له، والباطل قولهم اتخذ الله ولدا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yadmaghu means destroy; its root image is a head wound reaching the brain. Zahiq means gone, as falsehood vanishes when truth is made clear.
rows.anchor: {فيدمغه} فيهلكه، وأصل الدمغ: شج الرأس حتى يبلغ الدماغ، {فإذا هو زاهق} ذاهب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse threatens disbelievers for describing God with what is unfitting, such as a spouse or child.
rows.anchor: {ولكم الويل} يا معشر الكفار، {مما تصفون} الله بما لا يليق به من الصاحبة والولد.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses what they describe as their lies.
rows.anchor: والولد. وقال مجاهد: مما تكذبون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone in the heavens and earth belongs to God as servants and property; those near Him are angels.
rows.anchor: {وله من في السماوات والأرض} عبيدا وملكا، {ومن عنده} يعني الملائكة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels do not disdain or tire of worship; istihsar means becoming tired and exhausted.
rows.anchor: لا يأنفون عن عبادته ولا يتعظمون عنها، {ولا يستحسرون} لا يعيون،

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi explains that the angels do not act arrogantly toward worship.
rows.anchor: وأعيا. وقال السدي: لا يتعظمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels glorify God by night and day without weakening or tiring.
rows.anchor: {يسبحون الليل والنهار لا يفترون} لا يضعفون ولا يسأمون،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idol neither harms the worshipper if he abandons its worship nor benefits him if he worships it; this is far from truth and right guidance.
rows.anchor: إن عصاه ولم يعبده، {وما لا ينفعه} إن أطاعه وعبده، {ذلك هو الضلال البعيد}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent conflict is resolved by distinguishing no harm from abandoning worship from the harm caused by worshipping the idol.
rows.anchor: لا يضره ترك عبادته، وقوله: "لمن ضره أقرب" أي: ضر عبادته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying the idol's harm is nearer than its benefit follows Arab idiom: a nonexistent thing is called distant, as in a distant return; the idol has no benefit, while its harm exists.
rows.anchor: هذا على عادة العرب، فإنهم يقولون لما لا يكون أصلا بعيد، كقوله تعالى: {ذلك رجع بعيد}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One grammatical view treats the lām as extra, yielding whoever harms it is nearer; Ibn Masud reads it without lām.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم: هي صلة، مجازها: يدعو من ضره أقرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the phrase as to the one whose harm is nearer than benefit.
rows.anchor: وقيل: "لمن ضره" أي إلى الذي ضره أقرب من نفعه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parses yad'u as he says, with an omitted predicate meaning that the one is a god.
rows.anchor: وقيل: "يدعو" بمعنى يقول: والخبر محذوف، أي يقول: لمن ضره أقرب من نفعه هو إله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis supplies a second omitted yad'u, permitted by Arabic ellipsis after the first.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه يدعو لمن ضره أقرب من نفعه يدعو، فحذف يدعو الأخيرة اجتزاء بالأولى،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another takes the lām as emphatic: he invokes, by God, the one whose harm is nearer than benefit.
rows.anchor: وقيل: على التوكيد، معناه: يدعو والله لمن ضره أقرب من نفعه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another connects the first invocation to the previous verse's distant error, then begins a new clause with min as subject and labisa al-mawla as predicate.
rows.anchor: وقيل: "يدعو من" صلة قوله: "ذلك هو الضلال البعيد" يقول: ذلك هو الضلال البعيد يدعو،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawla means helper or worshipped deity; ashir means companion or associate, here the idol, and Arabs also call a spouse ashir because of close association.
rows.anchor: أي الناصر. وقيل: المعبود. {ولبئس العشير} أي: الصاحب والمخالط، يعني: الوثن، والعرب تسمي الزوج عشيرا لأجل المخالطة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Then We destroyed the others means We destroyed them.
rows.anchor: {ثم دمرنا الآخرين} أي: أهلكناكم.

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih says the rain that fell on them was sulfur and fire.
rows.anchor: قال وهب بن منبه: الكبريت والنار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The events are a sign, though most of the people did not believe.
rows.anchor: إن في ذلك لآية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the thicket are Shuayb's people.
rows.anchor: {كذب أصحاب الأيكة المرسلين} وهم قوم شعيب عليه السلام،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Iraqi readers hamz al-aykah here and in Sad; other readers pronounce laykah with open lām and tāʾ as a town name. All read it with hamza and kasra in al-Hijr and Qaf.
rows.anchor: قرأ العراقيون: "الآيكة" هاهنا وفي "ص" بالهمزة وسكون اللام وكسر التاء، وقرأ الآخرون: "ليكة" بفتح اللام والتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-aykah means a dense thicket of intertwined trees.
rows.anchor: والأيكة: الغيضة من الشجر الملتف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuayb is not called their brother among the people of the thicket because he was not related to them, but is called Madyan's brother because he belonged to them; God sent him to both groups.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل أخوهم؛ لأنه لم يكن من أصحاب الأيكة في النسب، فلما ذكر مدين قال أخاهم شعيبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prophets' calls share a form because they agree on piety, obedience, sincere worship, and refusing payment for preaching and conveying the message.
rows.anchor: وإنما كانت دعوة هؤلاء الأنبياء كلهم فيما حكى الله عنهم على صيغة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who reduce measures and weights diminish people's rights.
rows.anchor: الناقصين لحقوق الناس بالكيل والوزن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses completed the appointed term fully and finished it.
rows.anchor: قضى موسى الأجل} يعني أتمه وفرغ منه،

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says Moses stayed another ten years with his father-in-law after finishing the term, making twenty years in all, then sought and received permission to return to Egypt.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: لما قضى موسى الأجل مكث بعد ذلك عند صهره عشرا آخر فأقام عنده عشرين سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses traveled through a dark, intensely cold wilderness night while his wife went into labor.
rows.anchor: وكان في البرية في ليلة مظلمة، شديدة البرد وأخذ امرأته الطلق،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anasa means saw; Moses had lost the road and hoped to bring back news of it.
rows.anchor:
لعلي آتيكم منها بخبر}
عن الطريق، لأنه كان قد أخطأ الطريق،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A jadhwa is a piece or flame of fire; three vowel readings are reported: Asim opens jīm, Hamza dammas it, and the others kasra it.
rows.anchor: {أو جذوة من النار} يعني: قطعة وشعلة من النار. وفيها ثلاث لغات، قرأ عاصم: "جذوة" بفتح الجيم،

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada and Muqatil explain the jadhwa as a stick partly burned; its plural is judha.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة ومقاتل: هي العود الذي قد احترق بعضه، وجمعها "جذى"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taṣṭalun means that they might warm themselves.
rows.anchor: "جذى" (1) {لعلكم تصطلون} تستدفئون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mention of death reassures the emigrants: everyone dies wherever they are, so they should not stay in a land of polytheism out of fear of death.
rows.anchor: خوفهم بالموت ليهون عليهم الهجرة، أي: كل واحد ميت أينما كان فلا تقيموا بدار الشرك خوفا من الموت،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People return to God to be recompensed for their deeds.
rows.anchor: {ثم إلينا ترجعون} فنجزيكم بأعمالكم،

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr reads the verb in the third person plural masculine, yarjiʿun.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو بكر: "يرجعون بالياء".

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisai read nubawwiʾannahum with thāʾ unhamzated, from thawa, meaning to stay; the verb means to settle them in a dwelling.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة، والكسائي: بالثاء ساكنة من غير همز، يقال: ثوى الرجل إذا أقام،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other readers use the bāʾ form with fatḥa, doubled wāw, and hamza, meaning We shall lodge them.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون بالباء وفتحها وتشديد الواو وهمزة بعدها، أي: لننزلنهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghura f means elevated chambers.
rows.anchor: لننزلنهم، {من الجنة غرفا} علالي،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The patient endured hardships without abandoning their religion when distress struck; they rely on their Lord.
rows.anchor: {الذين صبروا} على الشدائد ولم يتركوا دينهم لشدة لحقتهم، {وعلى ربهم يتوكلون} يعتمدون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet urged persecuted believers in Mecca to migrate to Medina; they worried they had no home or property there and asked who would feed them.
rows.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال للمؤمنين الذين كانوا بمكة وقد آذاهم المشركون: "هاجروا إلى المدينة"،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A creature that does not carry provisions does not save food for tomorrow, like livestock and birds; God provides for such creatures and people wherever they are.
rows.anchor:
لا ترفع رزقها معها ولا تدخر شيئا لغد مثل البهائم والطير، {الله، يرزقها وإياكم}
حيث كنتم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears the believers say they lack resources to spend in Medina and knows what is in their hearts.
rows.anchor: السميع لأقوالكم: لا نجد ما ننفق بالمدينة، العليم بما في قلوبكم.

rows.speaker: علي بن الأقمر
rows.claim: Ali ibn al-Aqmar says the creature does not store anything for tomorrow; Sufyan adds that only humans, mice, and ants store food.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن الأقمر: وكأين من دابة لا تحمل رزقها، قال: لا تدخر شيئا لغد.

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reports that the Prophet said he had gone four mornings without food despite abundant provision being within God's power, chose alternating hunger and fullness, and warned of later people who stored a year's provision with weak certainty; the verse then descended.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: دخلت مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم [حائطا من حوائط الأنصار، فجعل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم]

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet did not store anything for the next day.
rows.anchor: عن أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: كان لا يدخر شيئا لغد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that day wrongdoers' excuses will not benefit them, nor will they be asked to seek a return or make amends in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: لا ينفع الذين ظلموا معذرتهم} يعني عذرهم، {ولا هم يستعتبون} لا يطلب منهم العتبى والرجوع في الآخرة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Kufans read yanfaʿ with yāʾ here and in Ghafir; Nafi agrees in Ghafir, while the others read it with tāʾ in both places.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة: {لا ينفع} بالياء هاهنا وفي "حم" المؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers say the Messenger and his followers are simply people of falsehood.
rows.anchor: ليقولن الذين كفروا إن أنتم إلا مبطلون} ما أنتم إلا على باطل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God seals the hearts of those who do not know His oneness.
rows.anchor: يطبع الله على قلوب الذين لا يعلمون} توحيد الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's promise to the Prophet of victory and triumph over his enemy is true.
rows.anchor: {فاصبر إن وعد الله حق} في نصرتك وإظهارك على عدوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not let those who lack certainty make you foolish or follow them into error; alternatively, do not let them unsettle your judgment and forbearance.
rows.anchor: {ولا يستخفنك} لا يستجهلنك، معناه: لا يحملنك الذين لا يوقنون على الجهل واتباعهم في الغي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says they should not make the Prophet's judgment and patience seem light; these people do not believe in resurrection and reckoning.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لا يستخفن رأيك وحلمك، {الذين لا يوقنون} بالبعث والحساب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luqman's son was called Anam, or, according to another report, Mashkam.
rows.anchor: لابنه} واسمه أنعم، ويقال: مشكم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For ya bunayya la tushrik, Ibn Kathir reads the yāʾ quiescent, Hafs with fatḥa, and the others with kasra; other ya bunayya forms in nearby counsel also vary by reader.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير: "يا بني لا تشرك بالله" بإسكان الياء، وفتحها حفص، والباقون بالكسر،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses weakness upon weakness as strain after strain.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: شدة بعد شدة.

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses it as weakness upon weakness.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: ضعفا على ضعف.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses it as hardship upon hardship.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: مشقة على مشقة.

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says pregnancy brings successive weakness and hardship to a woman; pregnancy, labor, and delivery each involve weakness.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: المرأة إذا حملت توالى عليها الضعف والمشقة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fisal means weaning; the child is weaned over two years.
rows.anchor: {وفصاله} أي: فطامه، {في عامين

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: Sufyan ibn Uyayna says praying the five prayers thanks God, and praying for one's parents after them thanks one's parents.
rows.anchor: قال سفيان بن عيينة في هذه الآية: من صلى الصلوات الخمس فقد شكر الله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to endure concerns harm suffered while enjoining good and forbidding wrong; these duties and patience under their harm are obligatory matters or matters one must resolve to fulfill.
rows.anchor: يعني من الأذى، {إن ذلك من عزم الأمور} يريد الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر، والصبر على الأذى فيهما،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, Asim, Abu Jafar, and Yaqub read tusaʿʿir with doubled ʿayn and no alif; the others read tusaʿir with alif.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير، وابن عامر، وعاصم، وأبو جعفر، ويعقوب: "ولا تصعر" بتشديد العين من غير ألف،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says not to be proud by belittling people and turning away when they speak.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يقول: لا تتكبر فتحقر الناس وتعرض عنهم بوجهك إذا كلموك.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says it refers to turning one's face away from someone with whom one has a grievance.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هو الرجل يكون بينك وبينه إحنة فتلقاه فيعرض عنك بوجهه.

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says it describes someone who twists his neck proudly when greeted.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: هو الذي إذا سلم عليه لوى عنقه تكبرا.

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas and Qatada say not to look down on the poor, treating poverty and wealth equally.
rows.anchor: وقال الربيع بن أنس وقتادة: ولا تحتقر الفقراء ليكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Marahan means swaggering; mukhtal is conceited in his walk and fakhoor boasts over people.
rows.anchor: {ولا تمش في الأرض مرحا} خيلاء {إن الله لا يحب، كل مختال} في مشيه {فخور} على الناس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Walk moderately, without swaggering or rushing.
rows.anchor: {واقصد في مشيك} أي: ليكن مشيك قصدا لا تخيلا ولا إسراعا.

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata interprets measured walking as dignity and calm, linking it to the description of God's servants in Furqan.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء: امش بالوقار والسكينة، كقوله: "يمشون على الأرض هونا"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lower one's voice means reduce its volume; Muqatil likewise says to lower it.
rows.anchor: {واغضض من صوتك} انقص من صوتك، وقال مقاتل: اخفض صوتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The donkey has the ugliest voice, beginning with a bray and ending with a sigh; these are also described as the sounds of the people of Hell.
rows.anchor: أقبح الأصوات، {لصوت الحمير} أوله زفير وآخره شهيق، وهما صوت أهل النار.

rows.speaker: سفيان الثوري
rows.claim: Sufyan al-Thawri says the cry of every creature is glorification of God except the donkey.
rows.anchor: سمعت سفيان الثوري يقول في قوله: {إن أنكر الأصوات لصوت الحمير} قال: صياح كل شيء تسبيح لله إلا الحمار

rows.speaker: جعفر الصادق
rows.claim: Jafar al-Sadiq interprets the verse's ugly voice as an unpleasant sneeze.
rows.anchor: وقال جعفر الصادق في قوله: {إن أنكر الأصوات لصوت الحمير} قال: هي العطسة القبيحة المنكرة.

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says Luqman articulated twelve thousand branches of wisdom that people incorporated into their sayings, judgments, and maxims.
rows.anchor: قال وهب: تكلم لقمان باثنى عشر ألف باب من الحكمة، أدخلها الناس في كلامهم وقضاياهم

rows.speaker: خالد الربعي
rows.claim: Khalid al-Rabi recounts that Luqman's master asked for the best and then worst two morsels; both times Luqman brought the tongue and heart, good or bad according to their condition.
rows.anchor: قال خالد الربعي: كان لقمان عبدا حبشيا فدفع مولاه إليه شاة وقال: اذبحها وائتني بأطيب مضغتين منها،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the trust is obedience and the religious duties God imposed, offered with reward for fulfilling them and punishment for neglecting them.
rows.anchor: عرضها على السموات والأرض والجبال على أنهم إن أدوها أثابهم وإن ضيعوها عذبهم، وهذا قول ابن عباس.

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud lists the trust as prayer, zakat, Ramadan fasting, pilgrimage, truthful speech, repaying debt, justice in measure and weight, and especially entrusted deposits.
rows.anchor: ابن مسعود: الأمانة: أداء الصلوات، وإيتاء الزكاة، وصوم رمضان، وحج البيت، وصدق الحديث، وقضاء الدين، والعدل في المكيال والميزان،

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the trust means duties and repaying debts.
rows.anchor: مجاهد: الأمانة: الفرائض، وقضاء الدين.

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya says it is what people are commanded and forbidden to do.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: ما أمروا به ونهوا عنه

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam identifies it as fasting, washing after sexual impurity, and hidden religious laws.
rows.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم: هو الصوم، والغسل من الجنابة، وما يخفى من الشرائع.

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
rows.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr says bodily faculties, beginning with sexual organs, are trusts from God; one who lacks trustworthiness lacks faith.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص: أول ما خلق الله من الإنسان فرجه وقال: هذه أمانة استودعتكها،

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Another view, transmitted by al-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas, defines the trust as people's trusts and keeping covenants, forbidding betrayal of believers or protected non-Muslims in any matter.
rows.anchor: وهي رواية الضحاك عن ابن عباس، فعرض الله هذه الأمانة على أعيان السموات والأرض والجبال،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and many early authorities say the offer was made to the actual heavens, earth, and mountains, who declined out of awe and fear of failing the trust, not rebellion.
rows.anchor: هذا قول ابن عباس وجماعة من التابعين وأكثر السلف، فقال لهن أتحملن هذه الأمانة بما فيها؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The offer was a choice, not an obligation; had they been compelled, they would not have refused. All created things submit to God.
rows.anchor: وكان العرض عليهن تخييرا لا إلزاما ولو ألزمهن لم يمتنعن من حملها، والجمادات كلها خاضعة لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage's submission of creation is linked to God's command to heaven and earth and reports of stones and creatures bowing.
rows.anchor: كما قال جل ذكره للسموات والأرض: "ائتيا طوعا أو كرها قالتا أتينا طائعين"

rows.speaker: بعض أهل العلم
rows.claim: Some scholars say God gave the heavens, earth, and mountains understanding when He offered the trust, so they understood and answered.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض أهل العلم: ركب الله عز وجل فيهن العقل والفهم حين عرض الأمانة عليهن

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the offer was addressed to the inhabitants of the heavens and earth, namely the angels.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: المراد من العرض على السموات والأرض هو العرض على أهل السموات والأرض،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the offer as directed to the inhabitants only, like asking a town means asking its people; Baghawi says the first view, addressing the entities themselves, is sounder.
rows.anchor: وقيل: على أهلها كلها دون أعيانها، كقوله تعالى: "واسئل القرية"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens, earth, and mountains feared failing the trust and being punished; Adam accepted after being told that good brings reward and evil punishment, and God promised practical help to guard sight, speech, and chastity.
rows.anchor: {فأبين أن يحملنها وأشفقن منها} أي: خفن من الأمانة أن لا يؤدينها فيلحقهن العقاب،

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says only the span between noon and afternoon passed between Adam accepting the trust and leaving the Garden.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: فما كان بين أن تحملها وبين أن خرج من الجنة إلا مقدار ما بين الظهر والعصر

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: A report ascribed to Ibn Masud by al-Naqqash compares the trust to a stone: the heavens, earth, and mountains declined, but Adam volunteered, carried it to his shoulder after successive trials, and God declared it a burden on him and his descendants until Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وحكى النقاش بإسناده عن ابن مسعود أنه قال: مثلت الأمانة كصخرة ملقاة، ودعيت السموات والأرض والجبال إليها فلم يقربوا منها،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains Adam as wronging himself and ignorant of God's command and the trust he undertook.
rows.anchor: {إنه كان ظلوما جهولا} قال ابن عباس: ظلوما لنفسه جهولا بأمر الله وما احتمل من الأمانة.

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says Adam was unjust when he disobeyed God and ignorant of the punishment for neglecting the trust.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: ظلوما حين عصى ربه، جهولا لا يدري ما العقاب في ترك الأمانة.

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says Adam wronged himself and did not know the consequences of what he accepted.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: ظلوما لنفسه جهولا بعاقبة ما تحمل.

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj and other language scholars offer two interpretations: humans bear duties and creation bears submission; or creation fulfilled its trust while the human bore it by betraying it.
rows.anchor: وذكر الزجاج وغيره من أهل المعاني، في قوله وحملها الإنسان قولان،

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: On the betrayal interpretation, Hasan says the human who bore the trust means a disbeliever or hypocrite who betrayed it.
rows.anchor: حكي عن الحسن على هذا التأويل: أنه قال وحملها الإنسان يعني الكافر والمنافق، حملا الأمانة أي: خانا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baghawī endorses the early authorities' interpretation of the trust as obedience and duties described above.
rows.anchor: خانا. وقول السلف ما ذكرنا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fearing God means obeying Him and avoiding disobedience; those who do good are believers who act well.
rows.anchor: اتقوا ربكم} بطاعته واجتناب معصيته، {للذين أحسنوا في هذه الدنيا} أي: آمنوا وأحسنوا العمل،

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil identifies the good promised in this world as Paradise.
rows.anchor: {حسنة} يعني: الجنة، قاله مقاتل.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the good as health and well-being in this world.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: في هذه الدنيا حسنة يعني: الصحة والعافية،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets God's wide earth as an instruction to leave Mecca, urging migration away from places where sin is open.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يعني ارتحلوا من مكة. وفيه حث على الهجرة من البلد الذي يظهر فيه المعاصي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says the verse was revealed about the migrants to Abyssinia.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في مهاجري الحبشة.

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Said ibn Jubayr says anyone commanded to commit sins should flee.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: من أمر بالمعاصي فليهرب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The patient held to their religion and did not abandon it because of persecution.
rows.anchor: {إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب} الذين صبروا على دينهم فلم يتركوه للأذى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says the verse concerns Jaafar ibn Abi Talib and his companions, who endured severe trials, kept their religion, and migrated.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في جعفر بن أبي طالب وأصحابه، حيث لم يتركوا دينهم لما اشتد بهم البلاء

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali says every obedient person receives a measured reward, while the patient are rewarded in heaps.
rows.anchor: قال علي رضي الله عنه: كل مطيع يكال له كيلا ويوزن له وزنا إلا الصابرون، فإنه يحثى لهم حثيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says people afflicted with trials will have no scale or record; their reward will be poured on them without reckoning, making people of ease wish their bodies had been cut because of that merit.
rows.anchor: يؤتى بأهل البلاء فلا ينصب لهم ميزان ولا ينشر لهم ديوان،

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says the negative particle is extra here: good and evil are not equal, such as patience versus anger, forbearance versus ignorance, and pardon versus wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: "لا" هاهنا صلة، معناه: ولا تستوي الحسنة والسيئة، يعني الصبر والغضب، والحلم والجهل، والعفو والإساءة.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says to answer anger with patience, ignorance with forbearance, and offense with pardon.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أمر بالصبر عند الغضب، وبالحلم عند الجهل، وبالعفو عند الإساءة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Responding in this way humbles an enemy until the former enemy becomes a close friend and relative.
rows.anchor: فعلت ذلك خضع لك عدوك، وصار الذي بينك وبينه عداوة، {كأنه ولي حميم}

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: Muqatil ibn Hayyan says the verse was revealed about Abu Sufyan, who softened after hostility through marriage ties with the Prophet and later became a close ally through Islam and kinship.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل بن حيان: نزلت في أبي سفيان بن حرب، وذلك أنه لان للمسلمين بعد شدة عداوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun refers to the virtue of meeting evil with good; only those patient in restraining anger and bearing harm attain it.
rows.anchor: {وما يلقاها} ما يلقى هذه الخصلة وهي دفع السيئة بالحسنة، {إلا الذين صبروا} على كظم الغيظ واحتمال المكروه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person of great fortune has great goodness and reward.
rows.anchor: {وما يلقاها إلا ذو حظ عظيم} في الخير والثواب،

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada identifies the great fortune as Paradise: only one destined for Paradise attains this virtue.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: "الحظ العظيم": الجنة، أي: ما يلقاها إلا من وجبت له الجنة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccans differed in what they said about the Qur'an and Muhammad, calling the Qur'an magic, soothsaying, or old tales and Muhammad a sorcerer, poet, or madman.
rows.anchor: في القرآن وفي محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، تقولون في القرآن: سحر وكهانة وأساطير الأولين،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says they were divided into believers and deniers.
rows.anchor: وقيل: "لفي قول مختلف" أي: مصدق ومكذب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those turned away from faith are people God has kept from believing in Muhammad and the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: يصرف عن الإيمان به من صرف حتى يكذبه، يعني: من حرمه الله الإيمان بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وبالقرآن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes ʿan to mean because of: the differing accusation causes some to be turned away from faith.
rows.anchor: وقيل "عن" بمعنى: من أجل، أي يصرف من أجل هذا القول المختلف

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains that the Meccans intercepted would-be believers, called the Prophet a sorcerer, soothsayer, or madman, and diverted them from faith.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنهم كانوا يتلقون الرجل إذا أراد الإيمان فيقولون: إنه ساحر وكاهن ومجنون، فيصرفونه عن الإيمان، وهذا معنى قول مجاهد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kharrasun are cursed liars, including those who divided up Mecca's routes and coordinated accusations against the Prophet to turn people from Islam.
rows.anchor: {قتل الخراصون} لعن الكذابون، يقال: تخرص على فلان الباطل، وهم المقتسمون الذين اقتسموا عقاب مكة،

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies the kharrasun as soothsayers.
rows.anchor: الإسلام. وقال مجاهد: هم الكهنة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghamra means heedlessness, blindness, and ignorance; sahun means heedless of the afterlife, the heart's attention having gone from it.
rows.anchor: {الذين هم في غمرة} غفلة وعمى وجهالة، {ساهون} لاهون غافلون عن أمر الآخرة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers ask when Judgment will come in mockery and denial.
rows.anchor: {يسألون أيان يوم الدين} يقولون: يا محمد متى يوم الجزاء، يعني: يوم القيامة تكذيبا واستهزاء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that day they are burned and punished in the Fire, as gold is tested in fire; ʿala can also mean with.
rows.anchor: {على النار يفتنون} أي: يعذبون ويحرقون بها كما يفتن الذهب بالنار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes ʿala as meaning bi, with or by the Fire.
rows.anchor: وقيل: "على" بمعنى الباء أي بالنار،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keepers of Hell tell them to taste their punishment, the very thing whose coming they demanded in this world while denying it.
rows.anchor: {ذوقوا فتنتكم} عذابكم، {هذا الذي كنتم به تستعجلون} في الدنيا تكذيبا به.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Amr, Hamza, and al-Kisai read the phrase with the mīm genitive, meaning among the people of Noah; the other readers use accusative, carried by the earlier sense of drowning Pharaoh and his army, which implies drowning Noah's people too.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي: "وقوم" بجر الميم، أي: وفي قوم نوح، وقرأ الآخرون بنصبها بالحمل على المعنى،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah's people were from before the Meccans, including the peoples of Ad, Thamud, and Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: أي: من قبل هؤلاء، وهم عاد وثمود وقوم فرعون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Flee from God's punishment to His reward through faith and obedience.
rows.anchor: فاهربوا من عذاب الله إلى ثوابه، بالإيمان والطاعة.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the command as fleeing from God to Him and acting in obedience.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: فروا منه إليه واعملوا بطاعته.

rows.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Sahl ibn Abdullah says to flee from everything other than God to God.
rows.anchor: وقال سهل بن عبد الله: فروا مما سوى الله إلى الله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As the Meccans called the Prophet a sorcerer or madman, earlier peoples called every messenger a sorcerer or madman.
rows.anchor: أي: كما كذبك قومك وقالوا ساحر أو مجنون كذلك، {ما أتى الذين من قبلهم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks whether earlier and later opponents advised one another to deny the message; its opening alif is reproachful.
rows.anchor: أي: أوصى أولهم آخرهم وبعضهم بعضا بالتكذيب وتواطؤا عليه؟ والألف فيه للتوبيخ،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says their rebellion over God's gifts and abundance drove them to deny the Prophet.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: حملهم الطغيان فيما أعطيتهم ووسعت عليهم على تكذيبك،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet may turn away because he delivered the message and did not fall short in his duty.
rows.anchor: لا لوم عليك فقد أديت الرسالة وما قصرت

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The exegetes say the command to turn away saddened the Prophet and distressed his Companions, who feared revelation had ceased and punishment was near; the command to remind them then reassured them.
rows.anchor: المفسرون: لما نزلت هذه الآية حزن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم واشتد ذلك على أصحابه، وظنوا أن الوحي قد انقطع،

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says to admonish Meccan disbelievers with the Qur'an; reminders benefit those God already knew would believe.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: معناه عظ بالقرآن كفار مكة، فإن الذكرى تنفع من [سبق]

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says to remind the believers among the Prophet's people, since reminders benefit them.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: عظ بالقرآن من آمن من قومك فإن الذكرى تنفعهم.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid compares the reckoning of the sun and moon to the measured motion of a millstone.
rows.anchor: ، قال مجاهد: كحسبان الرحى.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada say the sun and moon move on calculated courses and stations they do not exceed.
rows.anchor: يجريان بحساب ومنازل لا يعدوانها، قاله ابن عباس وقتادة.

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd and Ibn Kaysan say the sun and moon let people calculate times and lifespans; without the day-night cycle one could not reckon anything.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد وابن كيسان: يعني بهما تحسب الأوقات والآجال

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the sun and moon move according to a measure.
rows.anchor: شيئا. وقال الضحاك: يجريان بقدر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hisban can be a verbal noun like ghufran and kufran, or a plural of hisab like shubhan and rukban.
rows.anchor: والحسبان يكون مصدر حسبت حسابا وحسبانا، مثل الغفران والكفران،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najm means a plant without a stem; a tree has a stem that lasts through winter. Their prostration is their shadows, as in the Qur'an's description of shadows bowing.
rows.anchor: النجم ما ليس له ساق من النبات، والشجر ما له ساق يبقى في الشتاء، وسجودهما سجود ظلهما

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says najm means a star and its prostration is its rising.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: النجم هو الكوكب وسجوده طلوعه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky is raised above the earth.
rows.anchor: {والسماء رفعها} ، فوق الأرض،

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the scale means justice, as confirmed by the command not to transgress it.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: أراد بالميزان العدل.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan, Qatada, and al-Dahhak take the scale as the physical weighing instrument that enables fairness; its basic sense is measurement.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة والضحاك: أراد به الذي يوزن به ليوصل به إلى الإنصاف والانتصاف،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not transgress the scale means do not incline, oppress, or exceed what is right.
rows.anchor: "ألا تطغوا" يعني لئلا تميلوا وتظلموا وتجاوزوا الحق في الميزان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Establish weighing with justice.
rows.anchor:
في الميزان.
{وأقيموا الوزن بالقسط}

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Abu al-Darda and Ata explain the command as leveling the balance's tongue justly.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الدرداء وعطاء: معناه أقيموا لسان الميزان بالعدل.

rows.speaker: ابن عيينة
rows.claim: Ibn Uyayna says establishing the scale is by the hand, while justice is in the heart.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عيينة: الإقامة باليد والقسط بالقلب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not diminish the scale or defraud in measure or weight.
rows.anchor: ولا تطففوا في الكيل والوزن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is laid out for all the creatures spread across it.
rows.anchor: ، للخلق الذين بثهم فيها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fruit includes its various kinds.
rows.anchor: فاكهة} ، يعني: أنواع الفواكه،

rows.speaker: ابن كيسان
rows.claim: Ibn Kaysan says fruit refers to the countless blessings people enjoy.
rows.anchor: قال ابن كيسان: يعني ما يتفكهون به من النعم التي لا تحصى،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Palm-tree awkam are the sheaths that hold fruit before it splits; kam can mean any covering, including a sleeve or cap.
rows.anchor: الأوعية التي يكون فيها الثمر لأن ثمر النخل يكون في غلاف ما لم ينشق، واحدها كم،

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the awkam are husks or casings.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك: "ذات الأكمام" أي ذات الغلف.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says the palm's awkam are its fruit clusters.
rows.anchor: الغلف. وقال الحسن: أكمامها: لفيفها.

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the awkam are the spathe before it opens.
rows.anchor:
[وقال ابن زيد:
هو الطلع قبل أن ينشق]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Haqqa means the Resurrection, which has truly come to pass and cannot be denied; it also means the realities and recompense that become manifest and due.
rows.anchor: {الحاقة} يعني القيامة سميت حاقة لأنها حقت فلا كاذبة لها. وقيل لأن فيها حواق الأمور وحقائقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root haqq can mean that something becomes obligatory, as in the statement that the word of punishment became due against unbelievers.
rows.anchor: ولأن فيها يحق الجزاء على الأعمال، أي يجب يقال: حق عليه الشيء إذا وجب

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisai glosses al-Haqqa as the Day of Truth.
rows.anchor: قال الكسائي: "الحاقة" يوم الحق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What is al-Haqqa is a question that magnifies its importance, like asking who a great person is.
rows.anchor: {ما الحاقة} هذا استفهام معناه التفخيم لشأنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet could not know al-Haqqa because he had not seen it or witnessed its terrors.
rows.anchor: {وما أدراك ما الحاقة} أي أنك لا تعلمها إذ لم تعاينها ولم تر ما فيها من الأهوال.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada say al-Qariʿa means the Resurrection, which strikes servants' hearts with fear.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس وقتادة: بالقيامة سميت قارعة لأنها تقرع قلوب العباد بالمخافة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says Thamud and Ad denied the punishment promised by their prophets until it came and struck their hearts.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كذبت بالعذاب الذي أوعدهم نبيهم حتى نزل بهم فقرع قلوبهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamud were destroyed for their transgression and disbelief; taghiya may be a verbal noun or an adjective for their outrageous act, as in al-Shams.
rows.anchor: {فأما ثمود فأهلكوا بالطاغية} أي بطغيانهم وكفرهم. قيل: هي مصدر، وقيل: نعت أي بفعلهم الطاغية

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the taghiya was the overpowering cry that exceeded the usual measure of a shout and destroyed them.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: بالصيحة الطاغية، وهي التي جاوزت مقادير الصياح فأهلكتهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says the cry overflowed its keepers' control, as water overflowed against Noah's people.
rows.anchor: وقيل: طغت على الخزان [فلم يكن لهم عليها سبيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nabtali means God tests the human through commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: {نبتليه} نختبره بالأمر والنهي {فجعلناه

rows.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
rows.claim: Some Arab grammarians propose a reordered syntax: God made the human hearing and seeing in order to test him, since testing follows completion of creation.
rows.anchor: قال بعض أهل العربية: فيه تقديم وتأخير، مجازه فجعلناه سميعا بصيرا لنبتليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God showed the human the path of truth and falsehood, guidance and misguidance, and good and evil.
rows.anchor: {إنا هديناه السبيل} أي بينا له سبيل الحق والباطل والهدى والضلالة، وعرفناه طريق الخير والشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person is either a grateful believer and fortunate or an ungrateful unbeliever and wretched.
rows.anchor: {إما شاكرا وإما كفورا} إما مؤمنا سعيدا وإما كافرا شقيا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation reads the clause as a result: God made the path clear whether the person would be grateful or ungrateful.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معنى الكلام الجزاء، يعني: بينا له الطريق إن شكر أو كفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chains are prepared for the unbelievers in Hell, their hands bound to their necks, with blazing fuel.
rows.anchor: {وأغلالا} يعني: في أيديهم، تغل إلى أعناقهم {وسعيرا} وقودا شديدا.

rows.speaker: أهل المدينة
rows.claim: The people of Medina, al-Kisai, and Abu Bakr from Asim read salasila and qawarira with alif in pause and nunation in connected speech.
rows.anchor:
قرأ أهل المدينة
والكسائي، وأبو بكر عن عاصم: "سلاسلا" و"قواريرا" فقوارير بالألف في الوقف، وبالتنوين في الوصل

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza and Yaqub read these forms without alif in pause and without nunation in connected speech.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة ويعقوب بلا ألف في الوقف، ولا تنوين في الوصل فيهن،

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reads the first qawarir with alif in pause and nunation in connection, but salasila and the second qawarir without alif or nunation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير "قوارير" الأولى بالألف في الوقف وبالتنوين في الوصل،

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, and Hafs read salasila and the first qawarir with written alif in pause but without nunation in connection, and the second qawarir without either.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وابن عامر وحفص "سلاسلا" و"قواريرا" الأولى بالألف [في الوقف]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mutaffifin short measures and weights and withhold people's rights.
rows.anchor: {ويل للمطففين} يعني الذين ينقصون المكيال والميزان ويبخسون حقوق الناس.

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says they are called mutaffifin because the amount skimmed from a measure or weight is usually slight.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: إنما قيل للذي ينقص المكيال والميزان: مطفف لأنه لا يكاد يسرق في المكيال والميزان إلا الشيء اليسير الطفيف.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that when the Prophet arrived in Medina, its people were among the worst in measuring; after the verse came down, they improved their measures.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: لما قدم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة كانوا من أخبث الناس

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the verse was revealed about Abu Juhayna, who used one measure when buying and another when selling.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: قدم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة وبها رجل يقال له: أبو جهينة ومعه صاعان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording means when they take a measure from people; min and ʿala can alternate in this construction.
rows.anchor: وأراد إذا اكتالوا من الناس أي أخذوا منهم و"من" و"على" متعاقبان.

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says that when they buy for themselves, they take full measure and weight from others.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: المعنى إذا اكتالوا من الناس استوفوا عليهم الكيل [الوزن]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When measuring or weighing for others, they give less; Arabic may directly say I measured or weighed you, just as it may say I did these things for you.
rows.anchor: {وإذا كالوهم أو وزنوهم يخسرون} أي كالوا لهم أو وزنوا لهم

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda says Isa ibn Umar parses the verbs and hum as separate words, pausing after kalu or wazanu; Abu Ubayda prefers the unified reading.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: وكان عيسى بن عمر يجعلهما حرفين يقف على "كالوا ووزنوا"

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda prefers reading each verb with its object as one word: the manuscripts omit the alif that separated forms would require, and Arabic permits the direct construction kalatuka and wazantuka.
rows.anchor: أبو عبيدة: والاختيار الأول (3) يعني: أن كل واحدة كلمة واحدة لأنهم كتبوها بغير ألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yukhsirun means they reduce or shortchange.
rows.anchor: ووزنت لك. "يخسرون" أي ينقصون

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nafi says Ibn Umar warned merchants to fear God and give full measure and weight, because short-measurers stand at Resurrection sweating to halfway up their ears.
rows.anchor: قال نافع: كان ابن عمر يمر بالبائع فيقول: اتق الله وأوف الكيل والوزن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ala yaẓunnu means do they not know with certainty that the fraudulent will be resurrected for the great Day, the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: {ألا يظن} يستيقن {أولئك} الذين يفعلون ذلك {أنهم مبعوثون ليوم عظيم} يعني يوم القيامة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people rise from their graves to stand for God's command, judgment, and recompense.
rows.anchor: {لرب العالمين} أي لأمره ولجزائه ولحسابه.

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Umar transmits the Prophet's report that people stand before the Lord while sweat reaches halfway up the ears; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "يقوم الناس لرب العالمين حتى يغيب أحدهم في رشحه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Miqdad reports that the sun will draw near, people will sweat according to their deeds from ankles to knees, waists, or up to their mouths, and the Prophet demonstrated how some are bridled by sweat; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: المقداد صاحب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "إذا كان يوم القيامة أدنيت الشمس من العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers deny the Qur'an and resurrection.
rows.anchor: {بل الذين كفروا يكذبون} بالقرآن والبعث.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the denial they conceal in their hearts.
rows.anchor: {والله أعلم بما يوعون} في صدورهم من التكذيب.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses yuʿun as they conceal.
rows.anchor: من التكذيب. قال مجاهد: يكتمون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers who do good receive a reward that is neither cut off nor diminished.
rows.anchor: لهم أجر غير ممنون} غير مقطوع ولا منقوص.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada say kanud means ungrateful, denying God's blessings.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وقتادة: "لكنود": لكفور جحود لنعم الله تعالى.

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says kanud means ungrateful in Mudar and Rabi'a dialect, but disobedient in Kinda and Hadramawt dialects.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: هو بلسان مضر وربيعة الكفور، وبلسان كندة وحضرموت العاصي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says the kanud person counts calamities and forgets blessings.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: هو الذي يعد المصائب وينسى النعم

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata says the kanud person does not give to others during hardship.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء: هو الذي لا يعطي في النائبة مع قومه.

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses kanud as having little good, like barren land that grows nothing.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: هو قليل الخير، والأرض الكنود: التي لا تنبت شيئا.

rows.speaker: الفضيل بن عياض
rows.claim: Al-Fudayl ibn Iyad says one offense makes the kanud forget many good deeds, while the grateful person forgets many wrongs because of one good deed.
rows.anchor: وقال الفضيل بن عياض: "الكنود" الذي أنسته الخصلة، الواحدة من الإساءة الخصال الكثيرة من الإحسان،

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes say God witnesses the human being's ingratitude.
rows.anchor: [أكثر المفسرين] : (3) وإن الله على كونه كنودا لشاهد.

rows.speaker: ابن كيسان
rows.claim: Ibn Kaysan says the pronoun refers to the human, who testifies against himself through his actions.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان: الهاء راجعة إلى الإنسان أي: إنه شاهد على نفسه بما يصنع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khayr means wealth; shadid means miserly, as miserly people are called severe or hardened.
rows.anchor: لبخيل. يقال للبخيل: شديد ومتشدد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative reads shadid as strong: the person intensely loves wealth.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه وإنه لحب الخير لقوي، أي شديد الحب للخير أي المال.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baʿthara means to stir up and bring the dead out of their graves.
rows.anchor: {إذا بعثر} أي: أثير وأخرج، {ما في القبور} [من الموتى]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What is in the breasts is sorted out and exposed, including its good and evil.
rows.anchor: {وحصل ما في الصدور} أي: ميز وأبرز ما فيها من خير أو شر.

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jafar, Ibn Amir, Hamza, and al-Kisai read jamʿa with a doubled mīm to convey intensive accumulation; the others read it without doubling.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر، وابن عامر، وحمزة، والكسائي: "جمع" بتشديد الميم على التكثير،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAddadahu means he counted it; Muqatil says he prepared and stored it as provision, since the verb can mean keeping something back.
rows.anchor: {وعدده} أحصاه، وقال مقاتل: استعده وادخره وجعله عتادا له،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He thinks his wealth has made him immortal in this life and that his prosperity means he will not die.
rows.anchor: {يحسب أن ماله أخلده} في الدنيا، يظن أنه لا يموت مع يساره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla rebukes and rejects his assumption that wealth will immortalize him; yunbadhanna means he will be cast into al-Hutama, one of Hell's names like Saqar and Laza, called that because it crushes bones.
rows.anchor: {كلا} ردا عليه أن لا يخلده ماله، {لينبذن} ليطرحن، {في الحطمة} في جهنم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Hutama is God's blazing Fire that reaches the hearts; it consumes a person until it reaches the heart, and iṭṭilāʿ can mean reaching.
rows.anchor: نار الله الموقدة التي تطلع على الأفئدة} أي التي يبلغ ألمها ووجعها إلى القلوب،

rows.speaker: القرظي
rows.claim: Al-Qurazi and al-Kalbi say the Fire consumes all of the person until it reaches the heart.
rows.anchor: كل شيء منه حتى تنتهي إلى فؤاده قاله القرظي والكلبي.
